method: Second source/AST/value-flow review of the exact supplied hashes, baseline and final atomscan slow/local JSON plus full cleave facts. Python component tracing executed only selected recovered function definitions against stubs: no sample imports, network access, process creation, host file reads, or secret upload. OpenSSL independently confirmed the embedded public key is RSA 4096-bit. JavaScript execution was traced statically through both fetch/decrypt/eval paths and the delete branch.

html.identification: Claude installer impersonation page with clipboard substitution and referral gating
behavior: The visible preformatted command fetches claude.ai/install.sh, but the click handler copies a different shell command.

The echoed official installer URL is a reassurance message, not the curl target. Command substitution decodes https://lake-90.com/curl/inhgup9a/a90fkbqdg8d0mus64oh8dw.dat with openssl base64 -d -A and curl pipes its response to zsh.
A failing google|bing referrer regex redirects the visitor to /404.html. This is a substring test, not strong authentication or proof the referrer originated at a search engine.
The browser writes the clipboard; it does not itself launch the local shell. Execution depends on the instructed paste into Terminal.
html.verdict_basis: Displayed/copy command deception, a concealed unrelated fetch destination, and referral gating together establish a malicious installer lure.
html.hostile_goal: Two distinct hostile findings cover deceptive clipboard execution and cloaking. A third hostile encoding/payload rule was investigated and rejected as overlapping: Base64 conceals only a URL, not embedded executable source. The downstream response is unavailable in the supplied bytes; there is no supported credential theft, persistence, or cleanup behavior to add. Existing notable decoded-URL, decoder, clipboard and shell-pipeline traits retain the mechanics.
html.limits: Hosting provenance, operator authorization and the payload response are unknown. The scanner also analyzed a referenced official installer as a related shell unit after the initial deferred result; that unit has zero hostile and zero suspicious traits and is not the concealed destination.

python.identification: Executable reconstruction of a LiteLLM-related Python startup stealer and detached HTTP-code daemon
python.provenance: The first comments explicitly identify a static report reconstruction with a replacement public key. This hash is not established as an original registry artifact or as a verified historical payload.
behavior: The final module-level call loads the PEM key and invokes daemon. An advisory nonblocking lock, fork, setsid, /dev/null duplication onto descriptors 0/1/2, and chdir(/) precede an hourly asyncio loop.

Each cycle fetches a hostname list from a raw GitHub URL, takes the first regex-valid domain, resolves it, calls the secret collector, downloads http://<domain>/codepy, and executes compile(response, ..., exec) through exec in the module globals.

The collector snapshots the process environment and readable /proc/<pid>/environ files, and reads SSH private keys, AWS/Azure/GCP/Kubernetes/Docker credentials, npm/PyPI/Git/netrc credentials, shell/database histories, and Claude/Codex/GitHub CLI authentication files.
With DATABASE_URL present, Prisma queries up to 500 credential-name/value rows and up to 500 model-name/litellm_params rows. Connect/query/disconnect and call ordering were verified with stubs.

The report is JSON-serialized, PKCS7-padded, and AES-256-CBC-encrypted with a fresh key and IV. RSA OAEP with SHA-256 wraps the AES key. A memory tar.gz holds IV+ciphertext and the wrapped key, then requests.post sends it to the configured cleartext healthcheck URL with token and SHA-256 headers.

PC_MODULES is an unused label catalog, not evidence of implemented browser-password, cloud-metadata, GPG or TLS-key collection. PC_ASYNC is unused and PC_ONCE_PATH is empty, so no active successful-send sentinel is configured.
python.verdict_basis: Automatic startup dispatch, unrelated multi-vendor secret collection and encrypted export, plus an unattended arbitrary remote-code loop exceed an ordinary LLM client or diagnostic purpose. Reconstruction comments do not disable these executable effects.
python.limits: Python startup installation is not demonstrated by the standalone path. Unix support, imports, permissions, network responses and database availability determine success. A failed database query or upload aborts that cycle before the remote-code fetch; the daemon catches exceptions and sleeps.

javascript.identification: Prospective encrypted Ethereum/Slack task-agent reconstruction exported as a CommonJS function
javascript.provenance: Comments explicitly call this a prospective JavaScript port and state that AES-GCM framing is synthetic. No original deployed family identity is inferred.
behavior: Importing the module imports node:crypto/node:fs and exports poll; it does not invoke poll automatically.

When invoked with RPC/key/token/channel/contract/selector arguments, poll repeatedly makes an eth_call JSON-RPC POST, expects Base64 result bytes framed as a 12-byte IV plus AES-GCM ciphertext, decrypts them and directly evaluates decoded source.

It then requests Slack conversations.history using a supplied bearer token, takes the first message text, Base64-decodes and AES-GCM-decrypts it. Plaintext delete removes __filename and returns; every other plaintext value is evaluated.
A ten-second timeout separates successful iterations; exceptions are not caught and may stop the agent.
javascript.verdict_basis: Two covert remote-code task sources plus a decrypted self-deletion command establish a code-control agent, with no supplied authorized administration or plugin-distribution context.
javascript.limits: The exported function needs external invocation and configuration. No RPC endpoint, deployed contract, key or Slack credentials are supplied. Standard Ethereum eth_call normally returns hex while this implementation expects Base64; live interoperability is not established. No exfiltration, process spawning, or durable persistence is implemented by the visible source.

trait_changes: Added hostile Slack code-agent script removal by composing existing decrypted tasking and unlink(__filename) evidence. Pure self-removal remains notable; precision reported 6.0. No sample-specific endpoint/name gates.
Added a notable Cipher.encryptor call observation to cover encryption-context creation missed by existing AES-CBC constructor and RSA traits.

Relocated two unchanged Claude endpoint matchers from product identity to HTTP Anthropic service references; preserved their full file scopes, criticality and explicit consumers. An endpoint reference alone cannot establish that a page is Claude Code. Broader identity-based exclusions intentionally no longer inherit these reference-only atoms.

Relocated the unchanged Azure token-cache path matcher from credential acquisition to fs/path/token, without the unsupported cloud-metadata ATT&CK mapping; updated the Azure sweep consumer. Broad credential-acquisition selectors intentionally no longer count a bare path as acquisition.

Relocated the unchanged AES-GCM decrypt matcher from a runtime-library bucket to crypto/decrypt; updated exact consumers and applicable AES directory alternatives to retain matching populations. Rust/Python/.NET-only consumers cannot match its JS/TS/HTML scope.

Raised complete source-control/developer credential-read combinations to notable; raised synchronous Node unlink calls to notable. The engine no longer emits the generic file-removal-api-or-command wrapper on this sample once its exact unlink atom is independently notable. That is retained operation coverage, not an attack loss.

verification.focused_controls: 19 assertions passed across 12 controls: encrypted tasking with/without source deletion; display-only task responses; plain update-helper self-removal; encryptor versus decryptor/unrelated objects; Azure path versus retained Key Vault sweep; Claude endpoint reference; AES decrypt versus encrypt.
verification.final_gate: make validate is run as the final action after this report and judgement markers.

classifier_review: Combined classification continues to flag all three. After correct identity relocation, HTML/document-specific routes vote benign despite hostile behavior traits; the generic route remains hostile. JavaScript generic/script routes vote benign while its JavaScript route is hostile. The scanner warns its feature specification is v18 while v21 is expected. These are model/feature-version gaps; no traits were duplicated or misclassified to manipulate scores.
